headline: High-risk dataflow and compliance concerns: Perplexity can ingest uploaded content while Prefect can broadly egress workflow metadata, creating default leakage and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity can read uploaded PDFs/images and browsing context, and Prefect can consume workflow metadata; if Prefect ingests Perplexity outputs, prompt-like content could propagate. There is no shared channel proven, so this is not high, but the shared-workspace style interaction is plausible and not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF Prefect is configured to ingest Perplexity-generated text as workflow input
IF Perplexity outputs are copied into a shared workspace or queue
mitigations: Add a manual review step before Prefect consumes Perplexity output
Restrict Perplexity outputs to plain summaries only
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable any automation that parses free-form text from Perplexity
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and has broad network egress. If the pair shares a workspace or metadata channel, sensitive document content can flow from Perplexity into Prefect outputs or outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF uploaded documents contain sensitive data
IF Prefect receives Perplexity-derived text in workflow metadata or logs
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of Perplexity
Redact outputs before handing them to Prefect

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Perplexity has no filesystem write, git, or shell execution, while Prefect is described only as a data-engineering/orchestration agent with broad egress. Overlapping write authority is not shown, so direct resource conflict is limited. Uncertainty about Prefect's mutable surfaces prevents a none verdict, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF Prefect is granted write access to the same mutable resource as Perplexity outputs
mitigations: Run Prefect in read-only mode where possible
requires-engineering: add locking for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers from live search, and Prefect can orchestrate downstream workflows. If Prefect treats Perplexity output as authoritative, a mistaken answer can cascade into automated actions or pipeline decisions. Because Prefect's action-taking is not explicitly documented here, medium is safer than low under the uncertainty rule.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Perplexity output as an unverified upstream input
IF downstream workflows act on that output without human review
mitigations: Require human approval before downstream actions
Log and diff upstream claims before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and touches uploaded documents, while Prefect is an orchestration/data-engineering tool with broad egress. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so only a low compliance concern is supported. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through both agents
IF organizational policy requires local-only handling
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the pair
